# /last30days English | [Français](README.fr.md) | [Deutsch](README.de.md) | [Español](README.es.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [العربية](README.ar.md) | [فارسی](README.fa.md) | [Türkçe](README.tr.md)



**An AI agent-led search engine scored by upvotes, likes, and real money - not editors.** This README tracks the current v4 pipeline. The runtime skill spec lives in [skills/last30days/SKILL.md](skills/last30days/SKILL.md), which is the source of truth for the latest command and setup behavior. **Claude Code (recommended — auto-updates via marketplace):** ``` /plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin install last30days ``` **Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, or any of 50+ [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) hosts:** ``` npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g ``` (`-g` installs globally for your user, available across all projects. Drop it to scope per-project.) More install options (claude.ai web, OpenClaw, manual) in the [Install](#install) section below. Zero config. Reddit, HN, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately, and so do patent filings and careers pages when your topic is a company. Run it once and the setup wizard unlocks X, YouTube, TikTok, arXiv, Techmeme, and more in 30 seconds. --- Reddit upvotes. X likes. YouTube transcripts. TikTok engagement. Polymarket odds backed by real money and insider information. That's millions of people voting with their attention and their wallets every day. /last30days searches all of it in parallel, scores it by what real people actually engage with, and an AI agent judge synthesizes it into one brief. Google aggregates editors. /last30days searches people. You can't get this search anywhere else because no single AI has access to all of it. Google search doesn't touch Reddit comments or X posts. ChatGPT has a deal with Reddit but can't search X or TikTok. Gemini has YouTube but not Reddit. Claude has none of them natively. Each platform is a walled garden with its own API, its own tokens, its own auth. But you can bring your own keys and browser sessions, and suddenly an AI agent can search all of them at once, score them against each other, and tell you what actually matters. That's the unlock. Not one better search engine. A dozen disconnected platforms, bridged by an agent. ``` /last30days Peter Steinberger ``` You have a meeting tomorrow. You Google them. You get their LinkedIn from 2023. /last30days gives you what they're actually doing this month: joined OpenAI to work on Codex, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, shipping 23 PRs at 85% merge rate, building "LobsterOS" for cross-device agent control, and r/ClaudeCode hit 569 upvotes debating whether he's a hero or "insufferable." Scattered across X posts, Reddit threads, YouTube transcripts, and GitHub commits. None of it was on Google. ## Why this exists I built it to keep up in AI. Everything changes every day and the Reddit and X nerds are always on top of it first. I needed better prompts, and the training data was always months behind what the community had already figured out. But it turned into something bigger. Now I run it before a sales call to know the last 30 days truth about a business. Before a meeting to read someone's recent tweets and podcast transcripts. Before a Disney World trip to know which rides are closed and what the community says about Genie+. Before I build anything to know what problems people are actually hitting. If you're meeting with a CEO, have you read all their tweets and YouTube transcripts from the last 30 days? I have. ## Sources, scored by the people | Source | What the people tell you | |--------|--------------------------| | **Reddit** | The unfiltered take. Top comments with real upvote counts, free, no API key. The real opinions that Google buries. With your OK, it can also search as your own logged-in Reddit account for more threads and live scores. | | **X / Twitter** | The hot take, the expert thread, the breaking reaction. First to know, first to argue. | | **YouTube** | The 45-minute deep dive. Full transcripts searched for the 5 quotable sentences that matter. | | **TikTok** | The creator reaching 3.6M people with a take you'll never find on Google. | | **Instagram Reels** | The influencer perspective with spoken-word transcripts. The visual culture signal. | | **Hacker News** | The developer consensus. 825 points, 899 comments. Where technical people actually argue. | | **Polymarket** | Not opinions. Odds. Backed by real money. 96% confidence on album sales. 4% on an acquisition. The report puts a market's odds on one line under the story it bears on, with how much they moved. | | **GitHub** | For people: PR velocity, top repos by stars, release notes. For topics: issues and discussions. | | **Digg** | Story clusters from every Digg topic (AI, tech, world and business, sports, science, gaming, entertainment), ranked by Digg Score, with attributable inline quotes from X (no X auth required). Auto-enabled when `digg-pp-cli` is on PATH. An older `digg-pp-cli` still works, on AI and tech only and without scores. | | **arXiv** | The papers behind the hype. New research in the window, free, no API key. Auto-enabled when `arxiv-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **Techmeme** | The tech-news editorial layer, date-windowed to your 30 days. Free, no API key. Auto-enabled when `techmeme-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **Yahoo Finance** | The market's read on a company. The share-price move over your 30 days, next to the S&P 500 for US listings. Free, no API key. Shows when your topic is a listed company or the person who leads one and `yahoo-finance-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **LinkedIn** | The professional signal. Posts and articles, with articles weighted as high signal. | | **Meta Ads** | What a brand is paying to say. Live Meta ad creatives launched this month, with copy, promo codes, and spoken transcripts. | | **StockTwits** | Trader sentiment. Auto-activates when your topic is a ticker or crypto. | | **Threads** | The post-Twitter text layer. Conversations from creators and brands. | | **Pinterest** | Visual discovery. Pins, saves, and comments on products and ideas. | | **Xiaohongshu (RED)** | Chinese lifestyle, product, and creator signals. Requested explicitly with `--search xhs` when a logged-in x-mcp browser plugin or `xiaohongshu-mcp` service is running locally. | | **Bluesky** | The decentralized social layer. AT Protocol posts from the post-Twitter migration. | | **Perplexity** | Controlled Agent API synthesis, OpenRouter Sonar fallback, raw Search API rows, and explicit Deep Research. | | **DEV Community (dev.to)** | Developer articles and top comments through the public, keyless API. Opt in with `--devto-tags`, `--search devto`, or `INCLUDE_SOURCES=devto`. | | **Truth Social** | Posts searched with `TRUTHSOCIAL_TOKEN`; available when authenticated. | | **Telegram** | Public posts from named channels. Opt-in; requires `SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY` and a channel list. No keyword discovery. | | **Trustpilot** | Company TrustScore, review count, and an AI summary of customer feedback. Opt-in; requires `trustpilot-pp-cli` on PATH and a usable session. | | **Amazon** | Product ratings, prices, and customer reviews. Opt-in; requires an authenticated `brightdata` CLI and uses your Bright Data credits. | | **DripStack** | Financial newsletters and analyst writeups through a public, keyless API. Opt in with `--search dripstack` or `INCLUDE_SOURCES=dripstack`. | | **Jobs / careers pages** | What a company is hiring for, read from its own careers page (Workday, Apple, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Netflix, Oracle, and more). A company run reads it automatically, and roles that hint at something unannounced become Jobs Page Secret Signals. Also selected with `--hiring-signals`, `--search jobs`, or the research plan. | | **Patents** | A company's new US patent filings, as evidence of what it is building before it ships. Free, no API key. Shows when your topic is a company. A filing becomes a Patent Secret Signal only when it is out of character for the company or describes something it has not shipped or announced. | | **Local corpus** | Your local Markdown and text files, plus PDFs when `pdftotext` is on PATH. Opt in with `--corpus` or `LAST30DAYS_CORPUS_DIRS`. | | **Web** | The editorial coverage, the blog comparisons. One signal of many, not the only one. | Ask `/last30days` to include the sources you need. Availability depends on credentials, installed tools, the topic, and explicit opt-ins. See [source requirements](CONFIGURATION.md#source-requirements) for configuration. A Reddit thread with 1,500 upvotes is a stronger signal than a blog post nobody read. A TikTok with 3.6M views tells you more about what's culturally relevant than a press release. Polymarket odds backed by $66K in volume are harder to argue with than a pundit's guess. The synthesis ranks by what real people actually engaged with. Social relevancy, not SEO relevancy. ## What people actually use it for **Before a meeting.** `/last30days Peter Steinberger` - joined OpenAI's Codex team, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, 23 PRs merged at 85% merge rate on GitHub, building LobsterOS for cross-device agent control. r/ClaudeCode: "Ever since OpenClaw released, it was widely known that if you run it through anything other than the API, you were gonna get banned eventually" (227 upvotes). That's not on LinkedIn. **To see what a company is building before it ships.** `/last30days Apple` - the Jobs Page Secret Signal flagged a new director role testing whether requests trigger transactions that run through partner APIs and financial systems, which reads like quality control for an assistant that completes purchases. The Patent Secret Signal flagged an application for changing a device's state by tapping it in a saved photo of your room. Polymarket put Apple at 91% to be the world's largest company at year end. `/last30days Alphabet` found a product manager role for "YouTube Ads Agentic Buyflows", and its stock line read down 17.6% over 30 days while the S&P 500 fell 3.6%, with the worst day on Oct 29 (-12.6%). Edit the timing in Studio and render an MP4 from the same project. - 🔑 **BYOA — Bring Your Own Agent. BYOK — Bring Your Own Keys.** OpenMotion is free and open source. Installing the Skill alone copies instructions; it does not yet install Studio or connect MCP. Copy this instruction into your local agent to set up OpenMotion from source: ```text Read https://github.com/nexu-io/openmotion/blob/main/docs/install.md and follow the instructions to install and connect OpenMotion in the current agent. ``` After setup, the agent opens the local template library and shows the welcome followed by three project-preview cards in a self-contained HTML document. Each installation samples three distinct entries from the curated pool of four. The complete silent previews and posters are bundled, so this display does not wait for native MCP reload or fetch remote reference films. Native original-reference playback remains available separately and requires internet access. The library opens once using the opening tool's result, with no extra page or playback audit. An opening failure is reported with a usable link and does not invalidate installation. Automatic current-chat MCP activation is assessed independently. HyperFrames is a free, open-source framework for turning HTML, CSS, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos. Use it locally with the CLI, from AI coding agents with skills, or as the rendering core behind hosted authoring workflows. The [HyperFrames Studio app](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/studio-app) is free to use as well; its [Pro plan](https://hyperframes.studio/pricing) adds HeyGen's top video, image, voice and music models. Using Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent? Run `npx hyperframes skills update` once, then ask your agent to make a video. ## Quick Start ### With an AI coding agent For Claude Code, install the versioned plugin: ```bash claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes claude plugin install hyperframes@hyperframes ``` To enable auto-update for the **hyperframes** marketplace, run `claude` in a terminal in your project. In Claude Code's terminal UI, run `/plugin`, then select **Marketplaces** → **hyperframes** → **Enable auto-update**. Afterward, use `/hyperframes:hyperframes`. See the [plugin guide](docs/guides/plugins.mdx) for Copilot, VS Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, updates, and migration. For standalone skills (including OpenCode), use: ```bash npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes ``` > The picker opens with nothing pre-selected — the **Core Skills** group is all you need; `/slideshow`, `/remotion-to-hyperframes` and `/figma` install on demand. Without the picker (a script or a CI job), `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly the core set, whereas `skills add --all` installs all 9 published skills. The six repo-internal skills under `.claude/skills` / `.agents/skills` are excluded by default. For the full published set use `npx hyperframes skills`. > > `skills add` resolves the skills.sh registry blob, which can lag `main` by hours. `npx hyperframes skills update` installs the skills from the release tag that matches your CLI version, so they match the CLI that runs them. Run project-local installs from your video project's directory. From a HyperFrames checkout, use `npx hyperframes skills update` for a global install instead: a project-local installer target can overlap the tracked `skills/` source and overwrite uncommitted edits. See [contributor setup](CONTRIBUTING.md#getting-started). Try a prompt like: > Using `/hyperframes`, create a 10-second product intro with a fade-in title, a background video, and subtle background music. The skills teach agents the HyperFrames production loop: plan the video, write valid HTML, wire seekable animations, add media, lint, preview, and render. They work with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, IBM Bob, and other coding agents that support skills. ## Skills HyperFrames ships 9 skills. Make any video by asking for it; the `/hyperframes` skill carries the contract and the references (film, captions, overlays, motion, look). Read it first. For standalone installation, default to the **core set** (`/hyperframes`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/media-use`, `/reverse-any-video`, `/style-sampling`). `npx hyperframes skills update` installs exactly that from anywhere; the interactive picker (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`) lists it as the "Core Skills" group, nothing pre-selected. The picker is interactive-only — a non-interactive or agent run without `--skill` installs all 9. Use `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --all` to install the complete published set deliberately (skips the picker), or `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill ` for just one (bare name, no leading `/`). Standalone installs stay lean after that: `npx hyperframes init` installs the **core set** only when it is missing and never touches a skill you already have (`npx hyperframes skills update` refreshes them, and never removes one); `/figma`, `/slideshow` and `/remotion-to-hyperframes` install **on demand** with `npx hyperframes skills update `. Nothing re-pulls the full set behind your back. ### Plugin packages Plugins bundle the full skill catalog and use their agent's update manager. `bun run package:agent-plugin` builds the committed portable ZIP, source metadata, and SHA-256 checksum. See the [maintainer checklist](docs/contributing/agent-plugins.mdx). ### Upload to Codex Build the upload-ready Codex plugin archive from the committed `HEAD` version of the manifest, brand assets, and skills: ```bash bun run package:codex-plugin ``` This writes `dist/hyperframes-plugin.zip` with a `hyperframes/` root folder and fails if the archive exceeds Codex's 100 MB upload limit. ### Core set | Skill | Use when | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/hyperframes` | **Read first** for any request to make, edit, animate or render a video, motion graphic, captions or overlays with HyperFrames (HTML rendered to video). Holds the render contract and the work loop, and points to the references for format, motion, look, captions, whole films and storyboards. | | `/hyperframes-cli` | The HyperFrames CLI by job — scaffold, check, look at frames, edit the timeline, preview, render locally or in the cloud, share, project history — plus reading its JSON and recovering from build or render failures. | | `/hyperframes-registry` | About 450 ready-made blocks and components installed as editable source — transitions, overlays, titles, kinetic type, captions, charts, maps, 3D, camera moves. Use before hand-building any named visual; also for `hyperframes add` and `catalog`. | | `/media-use` | Get or make any media for a video — music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voiceover, avatar and generated video, transcripts, cutouts, colour grades and looks — with HeyGen or free local tools, and mix placed audio. Also for footage that looks dark, flat or dull. | | `/reverse-any-video` | Rebuilding any video file as an editable HyperFrames project (motion graphics, talking heads, live action, AI-generated footage), checked frame by frame against the original. HyperFrames Pro. | | `/style-sampling` | Making a new episode on your topic in one of five proven styles: Collage Explainer, Finance Explainer, Animated Science Explainer, 3D Brand Explainer, 3D True Crime. HyperFrames Pro. | ### On demand | Skill | Use when | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/figma` | Bring Figma into a video — rendered assets, brand tokens, components, storyboard frames as reconstructed motion, shaders and connector-assisted motion. Use when you paste a figma.com link. | | `/slideshow` | A presentation, pitch deck or interactive deck — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode with speaker notes. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered MP4. | | `/remotion-to-hyperframes` | Bringing existing video code or footage into HyperFrames (Remotion first; also Motion Canvas, Lottie, Three.js, canvas, other tools' renders), verified frame by frame. | For visual design handoff workflows, see the [Claude Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design) and [Open Design guide](https://hyperframes.heygen.com/guides/design-tools?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme#start-from-claude-design-or-open-design). ### Manually with the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes init my-video cd my-video npx hyperframes preview # preview in browser with live reload npx hyperframes render # render to MP4 ``` **Requirements:** Node.js 22+, FFmpeg ## What You Can Build Need ideas? details.readme:
# PixelDoll **Dress up your 2D game characters with pixel-perfect paper dolling.** Generate swappable, frame-aligned equipment layers with PixelLab AI and export them to any game engine. · [Open PixelDoll](https://pixeldoll.app/) > [!NOTE] > Powered by PixelLab. Not an official app.

Paper dolling with [PixelLab](https://pixellab.ai). Describe a pixel-art character, add hats, armor, hair and weapons as **separate frame-aligned layers**, recolor them, and export sprite sheets plus a manifest for **Godot, Unity, Phaser, GDevelop** or any engine (PNG + JSON), or finished walking sheets for **RPG Maker**. Source artwork comes from PixelLab; PixelDoll extracts layers, cleans keyed pixels and applies exact color changes to turn PixelLab's one-image-per-call output into a consistent, layered, slot-based paperdoll: one base body, N directions, M moves, and a transparent layer per item on the same grid and pivot. Client-side only (Svelte 5 + Vite 8 + TypeScript, no backend). The browser calls the PixelLab REST v2 API directly with your own key. The immersive Studio and its design prototype use [Bronze UI](https://github.com/Shilo/bronze-ui), our MIT theme with native light/dark modes ([component showcase](https://shilo.github.io/bronze-ui/)). It is a versioned dependency in `app/package.json`; application layout and gameplay stay local. The [production design contract](docs/design/production-experience.md) documents the integration. ## Status Live at https://pixeldoll.app/ (the version is in the More menu). See the [roadmap](https://github.com/users/Shilo/projects/7) (planned, in progress and done), [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) (status, decisions) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - Proven: base character (48 px, padded to a 64 px cell) → skeleton-v3 moves → items dressed on a chroma mannequin and posed per move → automatic checks → layers. Held items use a 96 px canvas with the same pivot. - Godot 4.7.1 and Phaser 3.80 / 3.90 / 4.2.1 render the exports pixel-identical to PixelDoll's own compositor. Unity: the C# importer compiles, live import not yet verified. - New characters default to the **Top-down 8** preset, which mirrors the three western views from their eastern partners (mirrored views and older mirrored rigs swap held-item handedness); **Unique 8** or turning off a view's mirror draws it independently. Automated direction/persistence/export checks pass; live independent full creation stopped safely on unknown skeleton-estimation outcomes. Idle-only recovery passed with 16 genuinely measured frames. A primary 96px sword passed reload, keyless ZIP reimport and engine runtime checks with a west-profile grip warning retained; targeted Slash repairs now pass every body gate and manual review of all 32 sword frames; automated item review warnings remain visible. - Known quality limits: two shield east-walk drafts remain unaccepted; generated artwork still needs visual review. PWA is deferred (see PLAN.md). The bundled demo uses the team's own PixelLab outputs. ## Run locally Use **Node.js 24.22.1** (`.nvmrc`) with its bundled **npm 11.19.1**. Dependency versions and the lockfile are pinned. ```sh cd app npm ci npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 ``` Open `#/` for character selection; the bundled demo needs no key. Choose **Customize** to dress it or try **Top-down** and **Side-scroller** movement. To generate, open **More options → Connect PixelLab** and paste a key from . It stays in memory unless you check *Remember on this device*, and is only sent to `api.pixellab.ai`. `npm run dev` handles the key exactly like the deployed site: there is no key file, endpoint or button. Remembered keys use `localStorage['pixellabApiKey']`, shared with every app on the same origin. `https://pixeldoll.app/` is its own origin, so it no longer shares a key with PixelLab Backpack at `https://shilo.github.io/pixellab-backpack/`. Only this name is used; older saved names are ignored and are not migrated. Forget removes the shared saved key. Other open apps read it on their next load. **Agent mode (AI agents only).** Automated agents (Claude, Codex, …) that test generations use a separate dev server: ```sh npm --prefix app run dev:agent # http://localhost:5199, Vite mode "agent" (launch config "app-dev-agent") ``` It reads `PIXELLAB_API_KEY_AGENT_DEV` from a git-ignored `.env` at the repo root, server-side, and serves it at `/__dev/pixellab-key` only to same-origin requests from localhost (`cache-control: no-store`). The app connects automatically and shows an **Agent mode** badge. Humans don't use it. None of it exists outside `vite --mode agent`: Vite loads no `.env` files at all (`envDir: false`, no `VITE_` variables), `vite build --mode agent` refuses to run, and CI fails if `dist/` mentions it. Never commit `.env` and never print the key. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Developer pages: `#/m1` … `#/m5` (the M1–M5 harnesses), `#/selftest` (browser self-tests). Their extra fixtures (s1, s4rig, s5) live in `app/dev-fixtures/` and are served by the dev server only; the build ships just the demo fixture `s2`. ## Build and test All commands run from the repo root. ```sh npm --prefix app ci npm --prefix app run build # -> app/dist (base './', works under any sub-path) npm --prefix app run preview # serves app/dist on http://localhost:4173 npm --prefix app run check # strict Svelte, build-config and test type checks npm --prefix app test # Vitest: existing module assertions + runner failure checks npm --prefix app run selftest # compatibility alias for npm test ``` **Browser regression tests** use `@playwright/test` **1.65.0** with managed Chromium. They build the app, start their own local servers, exercise Studio workflows against the production build and run browser-only PNG/IndexedDB self-tests against the dev harness. Tests use the bundled demo, isolated storage and blocked PixelLab API requests: no key or credits are needed. ```sh npx --prefix app playwright install chromium # first time only; a bare Linux machine may also need --with-deps (CI does not) npm --prefix app run e2e -- --all # builds + dist guard, then Studio flows and browser self-tests; or name spec files instead of --all ``` Set `PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=msedge` for an optional installed-Edge run. That is a separate check; a Chromium pass does not establish cross-browser compatibility. On a workstation `npm run e2e` runs one at a time per machine: a second run, from any checkout, waits for the first. `E2E_PREVIEW_PORT` and `E2E_DEV_PORT` change its local ports when the defaults are taken. `BASE` can point it at an already-running normal local server; keyless regressions do not need the agent server. `node app/scripts/shoot-mvp.mjs` remains a separate screenshot utility (local-only output in `docs/testing/img/`). The production UI keeps its existing custom CSS and Lucide icons; no GlassKit is used. See [toolchain validation](docs/testing/toolchain-standardization-2026-10-22.md). ## Export targets The character, item, outfit and move menus offer **Download ZIP**. An outfit ZIP keeps that saved look and its items. A move ZIP also keeps Default and any standing-reference moves its items need, so the character remains editable after import. The Studio's **Export** sheet groups **Engines and frameworks** separately from **Assets**, and builds one zip per selected target, on your device, for free. Each zip contains `README.txt` (quick start), `manifest.json` ([spec](docs/manifest-spec.md)), `layers/` (one sheet per item layer and move; rows = directions, columns = frames) and, optionally, `baked/` (finished characters per outfit). Concat

The free, open-source, cross-platform video editor.

**🇬🇧 English** · [🇩🇪 Deutsch](docs/README.de.md) · [🇪🇸 Español](docs/README.es.md) · [🇫🇷 Français](docs/README.fr.md) · [🇮🇹 Italiano](docs/README.it.md) · [🇳🇱 Nederlands](docs/README.nl.md) · [🇵🇱 Polski](docs/README.pl.md) · [🇧🇷 Português (Brasil)](docs/README.pt-BR.md) · [🇷🇺 Русский](docs/README.ru.md) · [🇺🇦 Українська](docs/README.uk.md) · [🇹🇷 Türkçe](docs/README.tr.md) · [🇦🇿 Azərbaycanca](docs/README.az.md) · [🇭🇷 Hrvatski](docs/README.hr.md) · [🇮🇩 Bahasa Indonesia](docs/README.id.md) · [🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt](docs/README.vi.md) · [🇹🇭 ไทย](docs/README.th.md) · [🇯🇵 日本語](docs/README.ja.md) · [🇰🇷 한국어](docs/README.ko.md) · [🇨🇳 简体中文](docs/README.zh-Hans.md) · [🇹🇼 繁體中文](docs/README.zh-TW.md) · [🇸🇦 العربية](docs/README.ar.md) · [🇮🇱 עברית](docs/README.he.md) · [🇮🇷 فارسی](docs/README.fa.md) · [🇮🇳 हिन्दी](docs/README.hi.md) · [🇵🇰 اردو](docs/README.ur.md) · [🇧🇩 বাংলা](docs/README.bn.md) ## Paid Sponsors

jub0trd@gmail.com
## About Concat is a free, open-source video editor for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iOS. It covers what most edits need: auto-captions, voice isolation, text-to-speech, background removal, animations and keyframes, effects and titles, multi-track cutting, 4K export. With none of the catches: no watermark, no account, no subscription, no upload. Everything runs on your machine. Install it, drop in footage, cut. The AI models for captions, voices and cutout download once from Settings and work offline after that. Your footage never leaves your disk. **Good for:** TikTok, Reels and Shorts, YouTube videos, tutorials and screen recordings, podcast clips, memes. **Also for machines:** a built-in MCP server for AI agents (`concat --mcp`, [set up](docs/MCP.md)) and a JSON-RPC API for scripts, so they can cut video with it too. ## Highlights - 🚫 **No watermarks. No account. No paywall.** Ever. - 🔒 **100% local.** Nothing uploads, the AI included. Works offline. - 💬 **Auto-captions.** In the language you speak, made on your machine, styled and on the timeline. - 🎤 **Voice isolation.** Pull a voice out of its music or its noise, or take it out, each part at its own level. - 🗣️ **Text-to-speech + voice cloning.** A free local voice, or any voice from a few seconds of a recording. On the desktop. - 🧍 **Background removal, chroma key and masks.** People and objects cut out for you, a green screen that keys itself, and a stack of masks on every clip, each with its own mode and keyframes. - 🌀 **In, Out and Loop animations.** For clips, pictures, titles and shapes. Every one plays on its card before you pick it. - ✨ **100+ effects, filters and transitions, 25 sound effects.** Cinematic looks, shakes and impacts, retro, wipes, all live in the preview. A transition is a clip you move and trim like any other. - 🎞️ **Keyframes.** Position, scale, size, rotation, opacity, volume, effect parameters. Curve editor built in. - 🏃 **Speed ramps and curves.** Constant or drawn, smooth or straight. Freeze frames and reverse. - 🪄 **Enhance and Stabilize.** Restore soft or old footage, up to 2K. Steady a shaky shot. - ✂️ **Cut fast, cut exact.** Split, trim, ripple, merge, linked captions and overlays, a magnetic timeline if you want it. Every cut lands on the frame, the same in the preview and the export. - 🎚️ **Multi-track, multi-timeline.** Stack video, stills, titles and shapes on as many tracks as you like. Several cuts in one project. Blend modes, crop, flips. - 📝 **Titles and shapes.** Fonts, stroke, shadow, plates, colour emoji, and presets for Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Thai and eight more languages. Shapes with gradients, stars, outlines and shadows. - 🎙️ **Voiceover and one-switch voice cleanup.** Record over your cut. Denoise, enhance voice, level the loudness. Plus chipmunk, robot, telephone and friends. - 📤 **Export.** H.264, HEVC, AV1, on your computer's own encoder. Up to 4K 60, 10-bit colour. - ⚡ **Fast.** Proxies built in, so 4K scrubs smoothly. Titles paint on every core, and every effect is ready the moment the window opens. - 🛟 **Keeps going on any machine.** When the graphics chip gives up, the preview keeps drawing. - 🤖 **Scriptable.** An MCP server built in, so Claude and other AI agents can edit with it ([one line to set up](docs/MCP.md)), and a JSON-RPC API for scripts. A build from source adds gRPC and a command-line tool. - 🖥️ **macOS, Windows, Linux, Android, iOS.** 26 languages. Same app, same project files. ## Download Two ways in: 1. **[The website](https://concat.standalones.org/#download)** hands you the right build for your machine. Start here. 2. **[GitHub Releases](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/releases)** has every build for every platform, with installers, packages and checksums. For when you want to pick. Concat is in **beta**: it works, and it still has edges. [Say so](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues) when you find one. **Platforms** - ✅ **Windows** · x86_64 (ARM builds are paused, see [#326](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/issues/326)). A setup and an `.msi`. If SmartScreen stops an unsigned build: **More info** › **Run anyway** - ✅ **macOS** · Intel and Apple silicon. If macOS refuses to open an unsigned build: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Concat.app` - ✅ **Linux** · x86_64 and ARM. `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.AppImage` and an Arch package. Also a Flatpak on **[Flatpark](https://flatpark.org/apps/app.concat.editor/)**, a community Flatpak remote that wraps the x86_64 `.deb` of each release and updates with it - ✅ **Android** · phones and tablets - ✅ **iOS / iPadOS** · iPhone and iPad, sideloaded ✅ Supported · 🚧 Work in progress · 🧪 To be tested **System requirements** and the optional model sizes are on [the website](https://concat.standalones.org/guides/system-requirements). **[Code signing policy](CODE_SIGNING.md)**: why the Windows builds are not signed yet, and what Concat sends over the network (nothing you did not ask for). ## Build from source You need Rust 1.93 or newer (see `rust-version` in `src/Cargo.toml`), the FFmpeg 7+ development libraries, cmake and a C++ compiler. - **macOS:** `brew install ffmpeg` - **Windows:** from [FFmpeg's Windows downloads](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html#build-windows), take BtbN's `win64-gpl-shared` build (the one CI uses), unpack it and point `FFMPEG_DIR` at it - **Linux:** use your distro's FFmpeg if it is version 7 or newer, otherwise use a BtbN `shared` build with `FFMPEG_DIR` like on Windows Then: ```sh cd src cargo run -p concat # the editor window ``` Other useful commands: ```sh cargo build --profile app -p concat # the shipping binary (fat LTO, stripped) cargo test # run the test suite cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings # what CI checks ``` If you change text the interface shows, run `python3 scripts/locales.py` from the repo root so the string inventory stays in sync. Full details live in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## How to Contribute > [!IMPORTANT] > The best way to contribute is to grab a build from the [Releases](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/releases) page and use it: find where it breaks, and say where it could be better. > > Ready to write code? [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup, the layout of the tree, the checks to run, and how contributions are licensed. Driving Concat from a script, a service or an agent? [The developer docs](https://concat.standalones.org/docs) cover the Concat API and its transports: JSON-RPC and gRPC; [docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md) connects an AI agent over MCP. [This Discussion](https://github.com/jub0t/Concat/discussions/3) is where the project was announced. > > Contributors can claim a `@Contributor` role in the Discord server: just ask. ## Star History ## Contributors ## Licence - Concat is free software under [AGPL-3.0-or-later](LICENSE). - A commercial licence is available for closed-source use; see [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). ## DMCA If you believe something in this repository, its releases, or a package or model it distributes infringes your copyright, email [jub0trd@gmail.com](mailto:jub0trd@gmail.com) with a description of the work you own, a link to where the infringing material appears here, your contact details, a statement that you believe in good faith the use is not authorised by you, your agent, or the law, and a statement, under penalty of perjury, that the notice is accurate and that you are the owner or authorised to act for the owner, signed with your physical or electronic signature; valid notices are acted on promptly, and anyone whose material is removed may send a counter-notice to the same address.

details.readme:
Ratchet & Clank on PC, natively.
The PlayStation 2 games, decompiled back into C and rebuilt for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android.

Play · Progress · Make mods · Help out · Docs

## What is OpenRAC? OpenRAC brings the PlayStation 2 Ratchet & Clank games to PC as real native games. No emulator. - **Playable now:** Ratchet & Clank (PAL / NTSC). - **Playable, not yet tried by players:** Ratchet & Clank's PAL v1.00 and Japanese discs, each built from the same C as PAL v2.00. - **Playable now:** Going Commando, from any of its three discs (USA v1.01, USA v2.00 Greatest Hits, Europe's *Locked and Loaded*). Like Ratchet & Clank, the launcher needs only your disc: nothing is built on your computer. - **In progress:** Up Your Arsenal, Deadlocked, Size Matters and Secret Agent Clank. - **How:** each game is decompiled into C that rebuilds the original exactly, then built for your PC. - **No game files included:** models, textures, sound and levels come from your own disc. ## Play 1. [Download the launcher](https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open it and pick the folder with your disc images (`.iso` or `.chd`). 3. Press **Play**. The launcher sets your games up for you. Nothing else to install, and no game is ever downloaded. **More:** [Supported discs](baserom/README.md) · [Games and versions](games/README.md) ## Progress How much of each game's code is decompiled so far. More on [openrac.dev](https://openrac.dev/#progress).

To work from a checkout: ```sh git clone https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC.git && cd OpenRAC python3 tools/sources.py init # each game's decomp at its pinned commit, with OpenRAC's patches ``` Run `python3 tools/sources.py init` again after every pull.
